prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which chemically designed molecules induce proximity between a chosen protein and the ubiquitin ligase machinery so that the protein is destroyed

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation as my single-part position. The scientific core is a transferable design rule: a heterobifunctional molecule brings a target and an E3 ligase together, and the ubiquitin system does the rest. Changing the warhead changes the target, so the principle is general and does not depend on a druggable active site. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the concept; Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turned it from a proof of principle into a rigorous, predictable chemical design problem. Independent reproduction is broad, solved ternary structures exist, and several degraders are in clinical trials. Having heard round 1, I would word the citation around induced proximity to the ubiquitin system, which is the principle, and not around PROTACs as one compound class. That lets the committee acknowledge the glue lineage without adding names beyond three, and I regard it as the honest way to state the credit boundary.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved, and I now weigh that more than in round 1, since Chabes and Aqvist both press it and the chair asks whether it differs in kind from the safety-maturity concern for base editing. I think it does: the chemical and structural validation is complete and the open question is clinical outcome, whereas for base editing the platform itself was recognised in 2020. Credit is still the weakest part of my configuration. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target and Sakamoto, Kim and Gray hold real claims, so a Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli prize will be read by some as leaving out the glue strand. B057 has four supporters, undisputed maturity and clean two-name attribution; my case rests on novelty of design principle and not on being the best-supported candidate.

responses.point: Johan treats Pd-catalysed C-N coupling as simple, general, enabling chemistry of undisputed maturity, and lists B004 as an alternative with Handa instead of Ciulli as the third name.
responses.response: I accept the maturity argument and it is the best reason to prefer B057. On the third name, I looked at your substitution seriously. Handa's cereblon identification is a real and distinct discovery, but it belongs to the molecular-glue mechanism, whereas Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli share one design concept, heterobifunctional induced proximity, with Ciulli supplying the structural chemistry that made it general. Putting Handa in the third slot would credit two different discoveries with one citation. If the committee wants the glue strand honoured, I think it is cleaner to say so in the wording of the citation than to rotate the names.

responses.point: Xiaodong argues that C-N coupling is chemically distinct from the 2010 prize because the problem is a different bond type and ligand design for reductive elimination from amido complexes, and admits that ranking it first favours a reliable workhorse over a field that created a new capability.
responses.response: Your own reservation is the point I would press. I now accept that C-N coupling is distinct from the 2010 work: the problem is different and the ligand solution is different. That moves me closer to B057 than in round 1, and I would no longer call it an incremental extension. Where we still differ is on what the committee should reward when both are mature enough. Degradation opens a new mode of action, event-driven rather than occupancy-driven, and gives biology a tool that did not exist. I would keep that ahead, but narrowly, and I would not object strongly to B057 winning.

responses.point: Andrei shares the Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli trio for B004 and names B058 and B057 as alternatives, while flagging that PROTACs and monovalent glues may be two discoveries.
responses.response: In round 1 I asked whether you weigh the missing approval as a timing risk. Your reply about two discoveries makes me think the stronger answer to the chair's question is to treat induced proximity as one principle. Both strands act by recruiting a ligase to a neosubstrate, and a citation worded that way covers the concept without naming Handa and Ito. If you think the glue strand is a separate prize, then B004 is better held for a later year than split badly, and I would want to know whether you would then move to B057.

responses.point: The chair proposes a two-part prize, B057 for Buchwald and Hartwig with B058 for Liu alone, and asks whether any other member supports a two-part configuration.
responses.response: I do not support the two-part configuration, though I understand why it has appeal. A B057 plus B004 pairing is not available under the three-person cap, because Buchwald and Hartwig already use two names. A B057 plus B058 prize would credit base editing to Liu alone and leave Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo out, and the CRISPR prize of 2020 and safety questions remain. I would rather the committee make one well-defined award than pair a mature method with a young one to broaden the appeal.

responses.point: Emma ranks biomolecular condensates first as a physical-chemical principle of intracellular organisation, and lists B004 and B058 as alternatives.
responses.response: I still respect the case and, as I disclosed, it lies close to my own field. Your own case against, that in vivo phase status is still contested and some evidence rests on overexpression or in vitro reconstitution, is the main reason I rank B004 above it. For degradation the molecular consequence is fixed and testable in structures and in cells, and the open question is clinical, not mechanistic.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a citation built on induced proximity to the ubiquitin system as an adequate way to acknowledge the molecular-glue lineage when Handa and Ito are not named
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes B004 premature this year compared with the mature B057
Whether Ciulli is the right third name or whether the committee would prefer a different attribution
Whether B057 should be preferred on maturity and breadth of support even though I weigh novelty of design principle more heavily
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent with any shortlisted candidate. My postdoc mentors (Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey) are not on the shortlist. My research overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly is scientific proximity to B051 and not a personal or institutional tie. I have no connection with Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Buchwald or Hartwig. My biosensor spin-out has no relation to any credited work.
